fix: Production defaults: theme.css.fast.load on, minifier on (never include portal-developer.properties in prod). Remove @import from page-set CSS.
where: portal-ext.properties · Pages ⚙ → Look and Feel → CSS

finding: Images are oversized or not compressed
fix: Select images from Documents and Media so Adaptive Media serves <picture>/srcset renditions. Define resolutions that match your breakpoints and run Adapt All Images.
where: Control Panel → Adaptive Media · Page Editor → Image Source: Direct

finding: LCP image not discoverable, lazy-loaded or not prioritized
fix: Keep the LCP image eager (Enable Lazy Loading off). Put it in the initial HTML (fragment editable, not injected by JS).
where: Page Editor → image → Enable Lazy Loading

finding: Where LCP time goes (TTFB, load delay, render delay)
fix: Reduce TTFB with fragment caching ("cacheable" fragments), production caches and the Page Audit panel's render times per fragment.
where: Page Editor → Page Audit · fragment.json cacheable

finding: Static resources have short or no cache lifetime
fix: Don't disable the Header/ETag filters (developer mode does). Put a CDN with origin pull in front.
where: portal-ext.properties · Instance Settings → General → CDN Host

finding: Slow document: redirects, server response, no compression
fix: Compress at the proxy/CDN, or turn on com.liferay.portal.servlet.filters.gzip.GZipFilter (it's off by default). Serve the site on its virtual host to avoid redirect hops.
Declare fonts through Style Book tokens. Self-host with font-display: swap, or use a system font stack.
Avoid CSS @import chains and JS that loads more JS. Use preconnect only for real third parties.

finding: Layout shifts: unsized images, injected content, web fonts
fix: Adaptive Media outputs width/height. Never inject banners at the top via JS. Use a page fragment (reserved space) or the native cookie banner (overlay).

finding: Third-party code blocks the main thread
fix: Move tags from the free-text JavaScript field to a JavaScript client extension (async/defer, versioned, scoped).
Build custom JS as client extensions that share Liferay's import maps (React, Clay) instead of bundling their own copies.
Paginate collections and Asset Publishers. Limit items per page and avoid nested grids inside collection items.
Terminate TLS with HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 at the reverse proxy or CDN (Liferay SaaS/PaaS do this at the edge).

finding: Tap delay because the viewport isn't optimized for mobile
fix: Keep the theme's width=device-width viewport meta tag. Don't override it in themes or client extensions.
Fix colours once in the Style Book (Primary/Secondary tokens) so every fragment inherits them.
Fill in Image Description on image editables and D&M files. Leave it empty only for decorative images (alt="").

finding: Icon-only buttons/links without an accessible name
fix: Expose aria-label as fragment configuration so authors set it without touching HTML.
Use Liferay Forms or Object form fragments (labels by default). In custom fragments, make the label configurable.
Set the Heading fragment's level for document structure. Control visual size with styles, not levels.
Configure site languages. Liferay writes lang on <html> per locale.
Give External Video fragments a title. Provide captions on hosted video.

finding: No way to skip repeated content
fix: Keep the theme's skip-to-content link and main landmark. Label nav landmarks via fragment configuration.
Remove dead snippets from the page-set JavaScript field. Monitor client extensions in each release.
Ask for permissions only after a user action, inside a client extension. Never in the global JS field.
Remove paste blockers. Use Liferay Forms validation and CAPTCHA instead.
Enable CSP with the [$NONCE$] placeholder. Start in Report Only mode, then enforce.
where: Instance Settings → Security → Content Security Policy

fix: Keep http.header.secure.x.frame.options on. Set HSTS/COOP at the proxy or CDN.
Terminate TLS at the proxy and set web.server.protocol=https so Liferay generates https URLs.
Let Adaptive Media pick resolutions per viewport. Define a high-density (2x) resolution where needed.
Use the native cookie consent banner and categorize cookies. Load tags only after consent.
Clear staging robots directives before go-live. Audit Robots per page and in robots.txt.
Set HTML Title and Description per page. On Display Page Templates, map them to content fields.
where: Pages → Configure → SEO · Display Page Template → SEO

fix: Maintain robots.txt per page set with [$PROTOCOL$]/[$HOST$]/[$PORT$] placeholders and a Sitemap line.
Make link text editable in fragments and write descriptive text in the Page Editor.
Keep Liferay's default absolute canonical. Use a custom canonical only for real duplicates. Pick the localized-URL strategy per instance.
where: Pages → Configure → SEO · Instance Settings → Pages → SEO

fix: Liferay generates hreflang per available language. Enable translated-pages-only to avoid pointing at untranslated pages.
Use real <a href> links in navigation fragments. Track 404s and create 301s in Redirection.
Reusable JSON-LD fragment (Organization/Product/Article), mapped to structure fields on Display Page Templates.

finding: Search engines can't discover all URLs
fix: Enable the XML sitemap per content type. In 2026.Q3, schedule cached generation for large sites.

finding: llms.txt missing required H1, links or length
fix: Enable the native llms.txt (2026.Q3 beta, flag LPD-80518) per site or instance and write curated Markdown: H1, summary, sections with links.

finding: Accessibility tree not well-formed for agents
fix: Same levers as accessibility: names, labels, landmarks and ARIA validity through Style Books and fragment configuration.

finding: Layout moves under an agent taking screenshots
fix: Reserve space for all content at render time. No JS-injected banners.

finding: Forms not exposed as agent tools
fix: Offer a fragment configuration toggle that adds WebMCP declarative attributes (toolname, tooldescription, toolparamdescription).

finding: No ai-catalog.json for agent resource discovery
fix: Keep an eye on the Agentic Resource Discovery spec. There's no native DXP feature yet.

finding: Agents need structured, permissioned access to content
fix: Enable Liferay's MCP Server (/o/mcp, flag LPD-63311). Agents act with the authenticated user's permissions.
